No explicit demand for a separate public page found in bounded official-source review; verify regulator guidance on this exact question. public_proposals.statement: According to PFRON (26 October 2026), there is no general requirement for a separate website accessibility statement. Covered service providers must publish accessible information about their service, its use and how it meets accessibility requirements in terms and conditions or an equivalent document.
public_proposals.reporting: PFRON states that Article 67 notifications have no specified deadline after discovery. Separate duties require manufacturers and service providers to notify the competent authority without delay in the circumstances of Articles 27(2) and 32(2)(6).
public_proposals.enforcement: In its reply of 26 October 2026, PFRON confirmed that accessibility market surveillance and monitoring had begun and that it was conducting compliance-monitoring activities. Inspections and administrative decisions were described as possible subsequent steps; no issued measures or outcomes were confirmed.
public_proposals.enforcement_detail: PFRON says optional dark mode can be assessed. Information about operators under surveillance may be requested under the Access to Public Information Act, subject to individual assessment and statutory restrictions, including business secrets.
